description: Our Team Name is Destination Moon, and we want to revolutionize how aircraft fly via microgravity, in terms of its oxidizer and fuel intake!
summary: Exothermic's is meant to be an interactive learning software, enabling students and mentors from around the world to learn how different situations might affect flame, both in gravity and in microgravity. We did it, by adding a bunch of models, and diagrams detailing in the fundamentals of flame, and going into how and why shape, color, and size are affected. We address the challenge, by implementing two specific ideas. The first section of our website is dedicated to finding how flame really functions, what affects it, diagrams showing it, models with sliders you can change to view how the flame is impacted and real-life examples. The second part is all our sources, our SI (super-intelligence). This is where you can compare all of the research spanning between all the 13 experiments or research papers we found. Additionally, for a more interactive experience we gave the opportunity to use these research papers and see how they might be used in different habitats. All, in all this website takes a small chunk which is significant, into one small area which allows us to both learn about how flame works, as well as organizing NASA's research and seeing how these experiments/ incidents aren't forgotten, yet must be used by generations, to not repeat such severe mistakes again.
details:
Our project is meant to give people, students, mentors, and everyone else a chance to understand how flame works weather in space, on earth, different chemicals, pressure, and even temperature affecting the flame. The way we have configured our project/ website is by giving numerous diagrams, and few models which have sliders, via which the user can learn how flame functions. Additionally, we have gathered research which is both beneficial to learn about as well implementing it in real-life scenarios. The main benefit is to make learning about flame easy, and also sorting out which experiment will be beneficial at any situation. The intended impact, is for both users such as students, educators to use this resource for learning, as well as NASA training, and using this website for their expertise as well as finding research from their countless experiments the found, clearly and efficiently. The creativity is presented in our project via the diagrams which we worked on very hard to create as well as the diagrams, to teach how flame works. In terms of factors, we mainly included the basic factors, such as who would this website appeal to, why does it work and how will we do it. In more detail for flame itself we have included a lot of creative concepts such as diagrams, and models, and a fire-based website, but since we also want to help NASA, we did include the history of failed crashes due to flame, and sources which NASA can use for their next trip wherever they go, whether its the moon, mars, or simply our space station.

Also, I really want to give a big thanks to Dr. Jain who pointed out many flaws and helped us fix all these bugs and errors.
